projects.title: Production automation at a property services group
projects.pitch: Five systems live in my first month, each with failure alerting and a written runbook.

projects.built: Three systems built and two taken over in month one, then more since.

projects.title: Power Platform proof: a PCF control and a Power Pages site
projects.pitch: A PCF field control that turns a due date into a live SLA countdown, and a Power Pages code site where patients of a fictional clinic request appointments.

number.label: automated tests pass across both projects, and both build clean
number.source: Public repo README, test runs on 21 Oct 2026.

projects.problem: Most Power Platform portfolios stop at screenshots. There is no code to read and nothing that proves the pro code side.
projects.built: A PCF control in TypeScript with green, amber, red and overdue states that all pass WCAG AA contrast, and a React Power Pages site on the Web API with POPIA consent, where signed in users see only their own requests.
projects.before: Low code claims with nothing to inspect.
projects.after: Two working projects with 57 tests each, solution packaging for the control, and deploy steps for a Dataverse environment.
projects.proofNote: The clinic is fictional and the site is not deployed to a live environment.

projects.title: Lead to deal copilot
projects.pitch: Inbound leads from a web form, email or Slack become clean, deduplicated HubSpot deals that a person approves in Slack with one click.

number.label: lost leads and 0 duplicate deals across 25 synthetic messages, through 12 HubSpot rate limit errors
number.source: docs/demo-output.txt in the repo, from npm run demo.

projects.problem: Leads arrive in three places and someone retypes each one into the CRM, so duplicates and gaps slip through.
projects.built: Claude cleans each lead, duplicates are caught before they reach HubSpot, and a person approves every deal in Slack.
projects.before: About 6 minutes per lead to read it, check HubSpot for duplicates, retype it and tell the team. That is an estimate, not a measurement.
projects.after: 25 inbound messages became 15 Slack cards that each need one click. Replays, spam and follow ups were handled without a person. 160 tests pass.

proof.label: Source, tests and the saved demo output on GitHub

projects.proofNote: Runs against mocks of Slack, HubSpot and Claude, so anyone can rerun it with no accounts. The AI answers in the demo are scripted, so it proves the plumbing and the fallbacks, not model accuracy.

projects.title: Missed call recovery kit for n8n
projects.pitch: A free n8n kit that follows up a missed call with a message and logs the lead for a callback.

number.label: missed callers got a booking link on a synthetic Friday, with 0 double texts and 0 texts after an opt out
number.source: docs/demo-output.txt and docs/e2e-output.txt in the repo. The same day passes 15 of 15 checks in real n8n in Docker.

projects.problem: A call missed during a busy hour is usually a lost booking, because nobody calls back in time.
projects.built: An n8n workflow that catches the missed call, messages the caller and logs the lead.
projects.before: A missed call at the dinner rush is a lost order. Nobody has time to call back.
projects.after: Every missed caller gets one text with a booking link, never between 21:00 and 08:00, and never again after STOP. The manager gets a counts only report at 08:00. 179 tests pass.

proof.label: Importable workflows, tests and the Docker run on GitHub

projects.proofNote: Free edition, MIT licensed. Fictional pizzeria, synthetic calls.

projects.title: Voice agent evals
projects.pitch: Regression tests for AI receptionists. Realistic caller scenarios run against the agent prompt before it goes live.

number.label: of 15 caller scenarios passed, weak prompt to fixed prompt, with the CI gate blocking the regression
number.source: docs/demo-output.txt in the repo, from make demo.

projects.problem: A prompt change can break a receptionist on calls nobody tested, and the first person to notice is a caller.
projects.built: A Python suite that replays caller scenarios against a voice agent prompt and scores every reply.
projects.before: A prompt change goes live and the first sign of a broken call is a customer hearing it.
projects.after: 15 caller scenarios run before every change, graded by code checks and an LLM judge, and a regression fails the build. 172 tests pass.

proof.label: Scenarios, checks, judge calibration and reports on GitHub

projects.proofNote: The 30 test calls in the repo are scripted, not recorded from a live model, and the README says so. Fictional dental practice and pizzeria.

projects.title: Grounded answers: RAG that cites and refuses
projects.pitch: An internal policy assistant over a fictional dental practice's documents that cites a source for every claim and says so when the answer is not there.

number.label: personal data leaks on a 50 question eval, naive retrieval vs hybrid search with guardrails. Must refuse questions went from 73% to 100% refused
number.source: docs/demo-output.txt in the repo, from make demo. The model answers are scripted for now, and the README says so.

projects.problem: A chatbot over company documents sounds confident even when it is wrong, leaks personal data it finds, and follows instructions hidden inside a document.
projects.built: Hybrid search (BM25 plus vectors in sqlite-vec) with a local reranker, a citation check that verifies every quote, refusals for low confidence and personal data, and defences against a planted prompt injection. A 50 question eval scores retrieval, citations, refusals, latency and cost.
projects.before: Naive vector search: 4 personal data leaks, 73% of must refuse questions refused.
projects.after: 0 leaks, 100% refused, 98% refusal accuracy, and every citation quote verified. 203 tests pass.

proof.label: Source, eval set and the method write up on GitHub

projects.proofNote: The reranker made multi hop retrieval slightly worse, and the README reports that instead of hiding it.

projects.title: Campaign brief agent: a checked multi agent plan
projects.pitch: Claude agents turn a marketing brief into a launch plan five teams can run, and a separate checker attacks the plan before a person approves it.

number.label: rubric checks pass on 5 of 5 synthetic briefs, and a planted prompt injection is flagged and not acted on
number.source: docs/demo-output.txt in the repo. The demo replays a recorded run and matches 840 of 840 events.

projects.problem: A brief becomes a plan by hand: split across teams, dates worked around weekends and approvals, gaps chased, then typed into Asana and Slack.
projects.built: Five specialist agents call validated MCP tools, a checker traces every requirement to tasks, one revision fixes what it finds, and approval is by exception. The dry run writes the exact Asana and Slack requests.
projects.before: Blocking findings at the first check: 36.
projects.after: Blocking findings after one revision: 1. 38 tests pass.

proof.label: Source, recorded run and offline demo on GitHub

projects.proofNote: Offline demo, no API key needed. Synthetic briefs and businesses.

projects.title: Parallel browser MCP server
projects.pitch: Gives AI agents many isolated browser sessions at once, so web tasks run side by side instead of one tab at a time.

number.label: faster on 8 slow pages: 22.86 s one at a time, 6.38 s with 4 sessions
number.source: The demo output in the repo README.

projects.problem: An AI agent with one browser works through pages one at a time, and two agents sharing a tab trip over each other.
projects.built: An MCP server over Playwright with isolated sessions, a session cap, per task timeouts, saved login profiles with a lock, and clean shutdown.
projects.before: 8 pages, one at a time: 22.86 s.
projects.after: 8 pages, 4 sessions: 6.38 s. 90 unit tests and the smoke test pass.

proof.label: Source, tests and the benchmark on GitHub

projects.proofNote: Runs locally over stdio. No network port.

projects.title: Receva: AI voice receptionist
projects.pitch: An AI receptionist on a live demo line takes orders and bookings for Harbour Slice, a fictional Cape Town pizzeria.
projects.numberNote: It runs on a demo line, so there is no client traffic to measure yet.
projects.problem: At the restaurant I managed, the phone rang most when our hands were fullest, and bookings rang out.
projects.built: A Twilio SIP trunk routes calls to a Retell voice agent. The agent's tools call the Receva site, which re-prices every order from the menu server side and sends the SMS confirmation.
projects.before: Calls missed during the rush, with no record of what the caller wanted.
projects.after: Calls to the demo line are answered with an AI and recording notice up front, priced from the menu and confirmed by SMS.
projects.proofNote: Harbour Slice and its menu are fictional, made for the demo. Call +27 87 250 3270 to try it.

projects.title: Receva: AI demo desks for prospects
projects.pitch: Per prospect pages where a stranger can question an AI receptionist, with no signup.
projects.numberNote: These are sales demos, so no business result is claimed.
projects.problem: Cold outreach had nothing interactive to show. A claim in an email and nothing to click.
projects.built: Each prospect gets a desk generated from their public business detail. The Claude API answers caller questions live, in that business's voice.
projects.after: A working desk the prospect can test for themselves. Nothing on it is scripted.

projects.title: AI engineering rig on Claude Code
projects.pitch: Custom subagents, MCP servers, hooks and scheduled agents that run research and checks in parallel.

projects.title: Agent Pipeline: multi agent document triage
projects.pitch: Four agents and a supervisor sort a pile of documents and log why each one went where it did.

number.label: routing decisions correct on a live run

projects.problem: Agentic AI is easy to put on a CV and hard to prove. I had nothing runnable to point at.
projects.built: A LangGraph state graph. Two agents read with Claude, two decide with plain Python rules, and a supervisor owns retry, escalation and degradation.
projects.before: Agent claims with nothing to run.
projects.after: A live run over 26 documents: 50 model calls, 301 audit events, zero retries. 267 offline tests cover the rules and routing.

proof.label: See all 26 documents and the raw audit trail

projects.title: DealFlow SQL: a PostgreSQL warehouse in one command
projects.pitch: About 1.5 million messy synthetic rows in, a tested star schema out, rebuilt by one command.

number.label: fact rows, with history kept as it was
number.source: Public repo. One command rebuilds it.

projects.problem: The source system keeps one status column and overwrites it, so nobody can say what share of deals reach an offer.
projects.built: A star schema on PostgreSQL 16 with Type 2 history, 84 monthly partitions plus a default, and bad rows diverted with a reason code.
projects.before: No history. Yesterday's status is gone by today.
projects.after: History reports as it was. 51 data quality assertions and 6 measured performance case studies, committed with real output.
projects.proofNote: Synthetic data only. Every query output, plan and buffer count is committed, so the numbers can be checked.

projects.title: DealFlow CRM: Dataverse built by script
projects.pitch: A Dataverse solution created through the Web API, then checked by a script that reads it back from the live environment.

number.label: checks passed against the live environment
number.source: Build log, Aug 2026. Walkthrough on request.

projects.problem: Most Power Platform work is clicked together in the maker portal. Nobody can review it, diff it or rebuild it.
projects.built: Idempotent Node scripts create the solution: 4 tables, relationships, alternate keys, 2 security roles, column security, 3 charts, a dashboard, a cloud flow and a published model driven app.
projects.before: A specification, runbooks and seed data. Nothing in an environment.
projects.after: The solution rebuilds from scripts, and each platform failure hit on the way is written up with its fix. Still to build: two business rules, an escalation flow and a canvas app.
projects.proofNote: Scripts and build log are on disk, with synthetic data only. Walkthrough and a live verify run on request.
